title: Bay Area Insiders Give Concerning Warriors Trade Update Amid Wendell Carter Jr. And Naz Reid Rumors
text:
Bay Area Insiders Give Concerning Warriors Trade Update Amid Wendell Carter Jr. And Naz Reid Rumors - BasketballNews NBA Play Hoops Rank NBA Play Hoops Rank Home / News Bay Area Insiders Give Concerning Warriors Trade Update Amid Wendell Carter Jr. And Naz Reid Rumors
 By
 Deblina Roy Nov 17, 2026, 6:11 PM CUT
 Imago
 IMAGO / ZUMA Press Wire
 While the Stephen Curry-barren Golden State Warriors are fixated on finding a new big hero who can step up and shoulder some of the responsibilities the superstar handled, the franchise’s prominent insiders and beat reporters Tim Kawakami and Marcus Thompson highlighted that the stakes are pretty high.
 The recent trade rumors involving the Charlotte Hornets star Naz Reid and Orlando Magic’s Wendell Carter Jr. may have looked like a light at the end of the tunnel. But that was until Curry’s right oblique abdominal tear, sustained during a game against the Houston Rockets on November 11. If landing Reid or Carter wasn’t a sweaty job already, the Golden State’s urgency to find an immediate replacement lessens the trade chances even more.
 “Obviously it’s a huge difference, and not knowing how long Steph’s gonna be out, but the cavalry’s not coming,” Kawakami said during a recent episode of the Warriors Plus Minus podcast. “They’re not getting anything for Porzingis right now … like, your urgency doesn’t make a trade easier. In fact, it makes it harder … Like, oh no, you got to do this; now we want two first-round picks …”
 Imago
 Golden State Warriors at Orlando Magic, Orlando, Florida, USA Orlando, Florida, USA, November 18, 2025, Golden State Warriors player Stephen Curry 30 and Draymond Green 23 at the Kia Center. Copyright: xMartyxJean-Louisx IMAGO / Marty Jean Louis
 Last week on his Clutch Scoops Show, NBA insider Brett Siegel emphasized Reid and Carter as potential prospects the Warriors could consider.
 “The two names that we’re paying attention to for the Warriors, that we have been paying attention to for months in terms of frontcourt talent, (are) Wendell Carter Jr.,” he said . “Naz Reid with the Charlotte Hornets … He’s had a ton of suitors between the Warriors, the Portland Trail Blazers, a few other teams mixed out there.”
 The Hornets’ center is averaging 17.2 points, 8.2 rebounds, and 2.2 assists, while Carter is going for 13.2 PPG, 8.8 REB, and 1.1 AST. Both could be the big-man scorers the Warriors needed with Kristaps Porzingis out. But it would still have been hard to make these trades more appealing at that time, considering both Reid and Carter’s performance for their respective teams.
 But the Warriors still could’ve tried their luck by throwing in some strong financial motivation via salary cap flexibility and a first-round pick. However, as Kawakami and Thompson stated, the Warriors’ urgency to land a trade will actually leave them with very little leverage to negotiate if they want a good big man. Other teams can easily hold the high ground and make excessive demands, which wouldn’t be the case had there been no urgency.
 Offering Draymond Green is a vague option, as the veteran forward is on a one-year, $27.7 million contract. However, it’ll break the core involving Curry, Green, rookie Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski. The team is already on an 8-6 record, after digesting two consecutive defeats from the San Antonio Spurs and New Orleans Pelicans in Curry’s absence. Losing more matches will cost them heavily, and Curry won’t be back to rescue anytime soon.
 So, with the Warriors stuck at the crossroads of losing their core, compromising their post-Curry future and needing an immediate fix, it’ll be exciting to see how the front office tackles the situation. But seemingly, they’ll have to take on the Dallas Mavericks on November 18 in their current lackluster state.
